analysis.purpose: The Go structural parser: turns the token stream into a declaration tree (func, method, struct, interface, typedef, type alias) plus a flat list of call sites, deliberately stopping short of a full expression parser because the symbol graph only needs declaration spans, nesting, and call-site heads.
responsibilities: Descend the token stream tolerantly, emitting a declaration per construct
Record nesting so members carry qualified names and member-of edges
Collect call sites in a separate whole-stream pass
Degrade on malformed input by skipping the construct rather than throwing
Nest interface methods inside their interface; everything else is top level, since Go has no nested type declarations

businessRules.rule: Not a full expression parser — a tolerant brace/indent-level descent is enough, and is far less surface area to get wrong.
businessRules.rationale: The symbol graph needs spans, nesting and call heads; parsing expressions would add risk without adding graph value.

businessRules.rule: Generic parameter lists use square brackets, so there is no angle-bracket ambiguity to resolve.
businessRules.rationale: Go syntax removes a whole class of parsing error present in Java and C#.

businessRules.rule: Struct and interface embedding is captured into bases so the resolver can emit inherits edges, even though fields are not symbols.
businessRules.rationale: Embedding is a real type relationship; a field is not.
